paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Obeying God can make things look WORSE before they look better. Moses and Aaron did exactly what the LORD sent them to do, and the next thing that happened was Pharaoh piling on more work (Exodus 5:7-9). If you ever did the right thing and your day got harder, you're in good company.

Look at what Moses does when it hurts. He doesn't hide and he doesn't pretend. He goes back to the LORD and asks, "Lord, why have You brought trouble upon this people? Is this why You sent me?" (Exodus 5:22). I think that's one of the bravest things in the whole passage, because he brought the hard question to the One who could answer it. Honest questions belong in God's presence, so bring Him yours.

And the LORD answers him: "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for because of My mighty hand he will let the people go; because of My strong hand he will drive them out of his land." (Exodus 6:1). Notice who is doing the work there. Pharaoh's hard heart doesn't get the last word, and neither does a hard season. When the straw runs out and the pressure rises, hold on, because the LORD's hand is still stronger than whatever is pushing on you.
